Although the triggers causing angiogenesis in the context of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) are not fully understood, oxidative stress is likely involved. Oxidative stress in the eye can occur through exposure of macular tissues to sunlight and local or systemic exposure to oxidative stressors associated with environmental or lifestyle factors. Because trace elements have been implicated as regulators of oxidative stress and cellular antioxidant defense mechanisms, we hypothesized that they may play a role as a risk factor, modifying the progression toward nAMD. Herein, we determined whether levels of human plasma trace elements are different in 236 individuals with nAMD compared to 236 age-matched controls without AMD. Plasma levels of 16 trace elements including arsenic, barium, calcium, cadmium, cobalt, chromium, copper, iron, magnesium, manganese, molybdenum, lead, antimony, selenium, vanadium and zinc were measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. Associations of trace elements with demographic, environmental and lifestyle factors and AMD-associated genetic variants were assessed. Elevated levels of barium and cadmium and reduced levels of chromium were observed in nAMD patients compared to controls. Mean plasma concentrations of barium were 1.35 μg/L (standard deviation [SD] 0.71) in nAMD and 1.15 μg/L (SD 0.63) in controls (P = 0.001). Mean levels of chromium were 0.37 μg/L (SD 0.22) in nAMD and 0.46 μg/L (SD 0.34) in controls (P = 0.001). Median levels for cadmium, which were not normally distributed, were 0.016 μg/L (interquartile range [IQR] 0.001–0.026) in nAMD and 0.012 μg/L (IQR 0.001–0.022) in controls (P = 0.002). Comparison of the Spearman's correlation coefficients between nAMD patients and controls identified a difference in correlations for 8 trace elements. Cadmium levels were associated with the smoking status (P < 0.001), while barium levels showed a trend of association with the usage of antihypertensive drugs. None of the AMD-associated genetic variants were associated with any trace element levels. In conclusion, in this case-control study we detected elevated plasma levels of barium and cadmium and reduced plasma levels of chromium in nAMD patients. An imbalance in plasma trace elements, which is most likely driven by environmental and lifestyle factors, might have a role in the pathogenesis of AMD. These trace elements may be incorporated as biomarkers into models for prediction of disease risk and progression. Additionally, population-based preventive strategies to decrease Cd exposure, especially by the cessation of smoking, could potentially reduce the burden of nAMD. Future studies are warranted to investigate whether supplementation of Cr would have a beneficial effect on nAMD. Highlights • Analyses of 16 plasma trace element levels in neovascular AMD patients vs controls. • Barium and cadmium are elevated in 236 cases compared to 236 age-matched controls. • Chromium levels are reduced in the neovascular AMD patients compared to controls. • Environmental and lifestyle factors affect trace-element levels in neovascular AMD. • Trace elements provide a potential target for novel strategies for AMD prevention. extracted_data.document_summary: This case-control study investigated plasma levels of 16 trace elements and 27 AMD-associated genetic variants in 236 individuals with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and 236 age-matched controls. The primary findings revealed significantly elevated plasma levels of barium and cadmium, and reduced levels of chromium in nAMD patients, suggesting that an imbalance of these trace elements, influenced by environmental and lifestyle factors, may play a role in nAMD pathogenesis. No association was found between the AMD-associated genetic variants and trace element levels.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Plasma levels of 16 trace elements (including arsenic, barium, calcium, cadmium, cobalt, chromium, copper, iron, magnesium, manganese, molybdenum, lead, antimony, selenium, vanadium, and zinc) were quantitatively measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in 236 nAMD patients and 236 age-matched controls. Two additional elements (Al, Ni) were initially measured but excluded due to inadequate accuracy/reproducibility. This was a cross-sectional, observational study, and no therapeutic interventions or dose-response comparisons were reported or applicable. Patients with nAMD may have received past anti-angiogenic drug injections, but details regarding dose, intensity, or duration were not the focus of this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean plasma concentrations were 1.35 μg/L (SD 0.71) in nAMD patients and 1.15 μg/L (SD 0.63) in controls (P = 0.001). In a multifactorial binary logistic regression model, Ba showed an Odds Ratio (OR) of 1.55 per μg/L for nAMD.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Trace element involved in the regulation of oxidative stress and cellular antioxidant defense mechanisms. Can inhibit potassium channels and Na/K pump in RPE cells, potentially reducing blood flow in the choroid and molecular transport across RPE membranes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), with a trend towards association with antihypertensive drug usage.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a potential role in nAMD pathogenesis, possibly through effects on blood flow and RPE function. May serve as a biomarker for disease risk and progression, and is associated with increased odds of having nAMD.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Median plasma levels were 0.016 μg/L (IQR 0.001–0.026) in nAMD patients and 0.012 μg/L (IQR 0.001–0.022) in controls (P = 0.002). In a multifactorial binary logistic regression model, Cd showed an Odds Ratio (OR) of 1.02 per ng/L for nAMD. Levels are significantly higher in smokers and consistently reported as higher in AMD patients (based on prior research).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Trace element that interferes with zinc metabolism, antioxidant and visual cycle enzymes, and enhances reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, leading to DNA/protein damage, inflammation, apoptosis, and angiogenesis. Implicated in increasing chronic oxidative stress and decreasing antioxidant defense systems.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), strongly linked to environmental and lifestyle factors, particularly smoking status. Accumulation observed in neurosensory retina and RPE of affected eyes.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a significant role in nAMD pathogenesis, contributing to cellular damage, inflammation, and angiogenesis. May serve as a biomarker for disease risk and progression. Strategies to reduce cadmium exposure, especially smoking cessation, could potentially reduce nAMD burden.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Mean plasma levels were 0.37 μg/L (SD 0.22) in nAMD patients and 0.46 μg/L (SD 0.34) in controls (P = 0.001). In a multifactorial binary logistic regression model, Cr showed an Odds Ratio (OR) of 0.09 per μg/L for nAMD.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Trace element involved in regulating oxidative stress and cellular antioxidant defense mechanisms. Has beneficial effects on RPE physiology, potentially increasing serum vitamin C and E and decreasing malondialdehyde levels, indicating antioxidant protection against lipid peroxidation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). No association found with demographic, environmental, lifestyle, or genetic factors in this study.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a potential protective role in nAMD pathogenesis; reduced levels could contribute to disease through loss of protective function and induction of pro-angiogenic pathways. May serve as a biomarker for disease risk and progression. Supplementation is suggested for potential beneficial effects on nAMD.
